newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELA PUBLIC SECTOR WORKFORCE KEEPS GROWING.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELA PUBLIC SECTOR WORKFORCE KEEPS GROWING.

text.p: Venezuela's bloated public sector workforce has grown by nearly six percent over the last two years, despite government claims that it was being gradually reduced, according to official figures.

The total number of public sector employees -- including state companies and regional government -- to June 30, 1997, was 1.355 million, up 77,853, or 5.7 percent from two years ago, according to Central Office of Statistics and Information (OCEI) figures. The public sector workforce was equivalent to 16.8 percent of the total workforce of 8.079 million.
Government officials have said the public sector payroll has to be reduced drastically to cut government spending and improve efficiency.
According to Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff, many public sector employees draw checks without actually turning up for work.
The government announced last week an incentive plan for public sector workers to take early retirement and voluntary separation.
Workers will receive a 50 percent severance pay bonus as part of the plan.
